quote.text: Our education system would be betraying its master, capitalism, if it taught us to be content with what we have. Or if it told us about the fruits of practicing minimalism.
quote.author: Mokokoma Mokhonoana
quote.aiInsight:
• Parenthood
    • Teach your children that true wealth lies not in accumulation, but in the cultivation of character and wisdom, allowing them to seek meaning beyond material possessions.
    • Encourage curiosity and resilience, helping them understand that while comforts are welcome, a balanced life is richer when experienced and felt deeply rather than simply owned.
  • Leadership
    • As a leader, recognize that the pursuit of profit can sometimes cloud judgment; strive to inspire your team to value integrity and purpose over mere accumulation.
    • Foster an environment where lessons in minimalism and measured ambition guide decision-making, ensuring that your leadership is driven by strategic vision and humanistic values.
  • Product Management
    • In product management, emphasize creating genuine value that transcends consumerism; challenge the status quo by questioning whether each feature truly serves the end user.
    • Adopt a minimalist approach in design and functionality, ensuring that products are not just commercial successes, but also enrich the lives of those who use them.
